title: TTNN cheat sheet for a decoder port

roots.tt_metal: tt-metal source tree at the coder image's pinned commit (python bindings, C++ nanobind files and ttnn python)

intro: Each signature was checked against the tt-metal tree the coder image is built from. Arguments not listed here do not exist. `python3 stages/2/stage_tools.py cheat NAME` prints one entry.

entries.name: ttnn.linear
entries.signature: ttnn.linear(input_tensor_a, input_tensor_b, *, bias=None, transpose_a=False, transpose_b=False, memory_config=None, dtype=None, program_config=None, activation=None, compute_kernel_config=None, core_grid=None)
entries.usage: y = ttnn.linear(x, w, bias=b, dtype=ttnn.bfloat16, compute_kernel_config=ck, memory_config=ttnn.DRAM_MEMORY_CONFIG)
entries.notes: x @ w (+ bias). The torch Linear weight is [out, in]: transpose it once at load (w_torch.T) or pass transpose_b=True. With no program_config the op picks one; start there.

entries.name: ttnn.matmul
entries.signature: ttnn.matmul(input_tensor_a, input_tensor_b, *, transpose_a=False, transpose_b=False, memory_config=None, dtype=None, program_config=None, activation=None, compute_kernel_config=None, core_grid=None)
entries.notes: Same as linear without bias. Batched matmul broadcasts the leading dims; both inputs must be TILE_LAYOUT.

entries.name: ttnn.MatmulMultiCoreReuseMultiCastProgramConfig
entries.signature: ttnn.MatmulMultiCoreReuseMultiCastProgramConfig(compute_with_storage_grid_size, in0_block_w, out_subblock_h, out_subblock_w, per_core_M, per_core_N, transpose_mcast, fused_activation, fuse_batch)
entries.usage: pc = ttnn.MatmulMultiCoreReuseMultiCastProgramConfig(compute_with_storage_grid_size=(8, 8), in0_block_w=1, out_subblock_h=1, out_subblock_w=1, per_core_M=1, per_core_N=56, transpose_mcast=False, fused_activation=None, fuse_batch=False)
entries.notes: Program config for a large matmul (prefill, interleaved). per_core_M and per_core_N count tiles per core; out_subblock_h * out_subblock_w <= 4. Skip it in a first port.

entries.name: ttnn.MatmulMultiCoreReuseMultiCast1DProgramConfig
entries.signature: ttnn.MatmulMultiCoreReuseMultiCast1DProgramConfig(compute_with_storage_grid_size, in0_block_w, out_subblock_h, out_subblock_w, per_core_M, per_core_N, fuse_batch, fused_activation, mcast_in0)
entries.usage: pc = ttnn.MatmulMultiCoreReuseMultiCast1DProgramConfig(compute_with_storage_grid_size=(8, 8), in0_block_w=2, out_subblock_h=1, out_subblock_w=4, per_core_M=1, per_core_N=8, fuse_batch=True, fused_activation=None, mcast_in0=True)
entries.notes: Program config for decode, where M is one tile row (batch up to 32).

entries.name: ttnn.WormholeComputeKernelConfig
entries.usage: ck = ttnn.WormholeComputeKernelConfig(math_fidelity=ttnn.MathFidelity.HiFi4, math_approx_mode=False, fp32_dest_acc_en=True, packer_l1_acc=True)   # lower: math_fidelity=ttnn.MathFidelity.LoFi, math_approx_mode=True, fp32_dest_acc_en=False
entries.notes: Precision of a matmul or norm. HiFi4 with fp32 accumulation is the safe choice while matching the CPU reference; lower fidelity comes after the check passes. Blackhole uses the same class. LoFi with approximate math ran on a Blackhole chip in probe 17 for matmuls with bfp4 weights and kept PCC 0.9999 against HiFi4.

entries.name: ttnn.rms_norm
entries.signature: ttnn.rms_norm(input_tensor, *, epsilon=1e-12, weight=None, bias=None, residual_input_tensor=None, memory_config=None, program_config=None, compute_kernel_config=None)
entries.notes: Set epsilon from the config; the default 1e-12 is rarely right. A ROW_MAJOR weight needs last dim 32 ([1, 1, hidden/32, 32]); a TILE weight needs the input's last dim. If the reference adds 1 to the weight, add it at load. The keywords are epsilon and weight.

entries.name: ttnn.softmax
entries.notes: Use numeric_stable=True for attention scores built by hand.

entries.name: ttnn.embedding
entries.signature: ttnn.embedding(input_tensor, weight, *, padding_idx=None, layout=None, embeddings_type=None, dtype=None, memory_config=None)
entries.notes: ids are uint32 ROW_MAJOR; the weight is the [vocab, hidden] table in ROW_MAJOR. The keyword is `weight`; `weights` is an error. Without layout=TILE_LAYOUT the output is row major.

entries.name: ttnn.from_torch
entries.signature: ttnn.from_torch(tensor, dtype=None, layout=None, device=None, memory_config=None, mesh_mapper=None)
entries.notes: Host torch tensor to device. Weights go in TILE_LAYOUT; token ids for an embedding go in ROW_MAJOR_LAYOUT as uint32. On a mesh the result is distributed: ttnn.to_torch needs a mesh_composer (run 20: "Can't convert a tensor distributed on MeshShape([1, 2]) mesh ... Supply a mesh composer"). With no mapper it replicates (measured on 1 x 2: two device tensors, each equal to the input), like ReplicateTensorToMesh; a sharded layout needs ShardTensorToMesh. Issue 563.

entries.name: ttnn.to_torch
entries.notes: Device tensor to torch. With a mesh the composer joins the per-device shards; replicated tensors then repeat, so take the first copy. The result is padded to tiles: slice to the real length.

entries.name: ttnn.as_tensor
entries.signature: ttnn.as_tensor(tensor, dtype=None, layout=None, device=None, memory_config=None, mesh_mapper=None, cache_file_name=None)
entries.usage: w = ttnn.as_tensor(w_torch, dtype=ttnn.bfloat16, device=mesh_device, layout=ttnn.TILE_LAYOUT, memory_config=ttnn.DRAM_MEMORY_CONFIG)
entries.notes: Like from_torch, and can cache the converted weight on disk with cache_file_name.

entries.name: ttnn.to_layout
entries.notes: Changes TILE_LAYOUT and ROW_MAJOR_LAYOUT. Matmul, rms_norm and attention need TILE_LAYOUT; embedding ids and reshapes of odd shapes need ROW_MAJOR_LAYOUT.

entries.name: ttnn.typecast
entries.notes: Changes dtype on the device. Rotary embedding and attention want bfloat16 inputs; bfloat8_b is for weights and some activations.

entries.name: ttnn.reshape
entries.notes: Shapes are 4-D by convention in the reference ports: (1, 1, tokens, features). The last two dims are padded to 32.

entries.name: ttnn.permute
entries.notes: Reorders every dimension (dims names all of them). The head split of a projection is reshape to [1, S, heads, hd] then permute (0, 2, 1, 3) to [1, heads, S, hd]; the way back is the same permute and a reshape to [1, 1, S, heads * hd]. Run on a chip by op probe 9 (head_permute, PCC 1.0) and probe 8 (the output join). dims lists one entry per axis of the input, so a 4-D tensor takes four numbers and a 5-D tensor five. A ttnn tensor has no .permute method.

entries.name: ttnn.relu
entries.notes: Elementwise max(x, 0). The Qwen4 indexer scores each key block with relu(q . block key) summed over the index heads; exact zeros are common, so the scores tie (see ttnn.topk). Run on a chip by op probe 9 (index_scores, PCC 0.99998).

entries.name: ttnn.transpose
entries.notes: Swaps two dims.

entries.name: ttnn.neg
entries.notes: ttnn.Tensor defines +, -, * and / with another tensor or a number, and no unary minus: `-x` raises TypeError. Use ttnn.neg(x) or ttnn.multiply(x, -1.0). Rotate-half is ttnn.concat([ttnn.neg(x2), x1], dim=-1).
entries.seen_in: tt-metal ttnn/cpp/ttnn/operations/eltwise/unary/unary_nanobind.cpp (bind_unary_operation_subcoregrids neg); ttnn/ttnn/__init__.py lists the Tensor operators

entries.name: ttnn.repeat
entries.notes: repeat_dims is one tuple with a count for each dimension: here the last dimension is repeated 4 times. ttnn.repeat(x, 1, 1, 1, 4), one argument per dimension, fails with 'incompatible function arguments'.

entries.name: ttnn.concat
entries.notes: Joins a list of tensors along one dim.

entries.name: ttnn.slice
entries.notes: Returns the part between the start and end indices (end exclusive), one index per dimension. Every start must be below the dimension and every end at most the dimension; a slice outside the padded shape fails with TT_FATAL.

entries.name: ttnn.sigmoid
entries.notes: Elementwise logistic function. The Qwen4 gated residual runs it on the up-projection of the mix weights and on the injection weights (op probe 4 matched the torch module at PCC 0.9999 on one chip).

entries.name: ttnn.softplus
entries.signature: ttnn.softplus(input_tensor, *, beta=1.0, threshold=20.0, memory_config=None, output_tensor=None, sub_core_grids=None)
entries.notes: Elementwise log(1 + exp(beta * x)); the defaults match torch.nn.functional.softplus. The Qwen4 gated delta net runs it on the time-step projection plus its bias to make the decay. Not run on a chip by a probe of this repository yet.

entries.name: ttnn.abs
entries.notes: Elementwise |x|. Not chip-tested here.

entries.name: ttnn.sign
entries.notes: Elementwise sign (-1, 0, 1). Not chip-tested here.

entries.name: ttnn.sqrt
entries.notes: Elementwise square root. Not chip-tested here.

entries.name: ttnn.clamp
entries.notes: Elementwise clamp; min and max are floats. Not chip-tested here.

entries.name: ttnn.sum
entries.signature: ttnn.sum(input_tensor, dim=None, keepdim=False, *, memory_config=None, compute_kernel_config=None, scalar=1.0, correction=None, sub_core_grids=None, fast_and_approximate_mode=False, output_layout=None)
entries.notes: Sum over dim; keepdim=True keeps it with size 1. Not chip-tested here.

entries.name: ttnn.multiply
entries.usage: y = ttnn.multiply(gate, up)   # or, with silu applied to gate inside the op: ttnn.multiply(gate, up, input_tensor_a_activations=[ttnn.UnaryOpType.SILU])
entries.notes: Elementwise product; b may be a Python scalar. add, subtract and silu are called the same way. input_tensor_a_activations=[ttnn.UnaryOpType.SILU] applies silu to the first input inside the multiply, which saves one op (it ran on a Blackhole chip in probe 17 with the same result as a separate silu).

entries.name: ttnn.silu
entries.notes: Activation for the gated MLP: down(silu(gate) * up).

entries.name: ttnn.deallocate
entries.notes: Frees a device tensor you no longer need. Needed inside a layer loop on a small chip.

entries.name: ttnn.TILE_LAYOUT
entries.notes: 32x32 tile layout. Dtypes: ttnn.bfloat16, ttnn.bfloat8_b, ttnn.uint32, ttnn.int32.

entries.name: ttnn.ROW_MAJOR_LAYOUT
entries.notes: Layout for token ids. Pair it with ttnn.uint32.

entries.name: ttnn.experimental.rotary_embedding_llama
entries.signature: ttnn.experimental.rotary_embedding_llama(input_tensor, cos_cache, sin_cache, trans_mat, is_decode_mode=False, memory_config=None, compute_kernel_config=None)
entries.notes: Rotation for the Llama pairing (rotate_half layout). cos and sin are [1, 1, seq, head_dim]; trans_mat is a 32x32 transformation matrix built once (see rope.py). The op rotates a whole head: when partial_rotary_factor is below 1, split the head, rotate the first head_dim * factor values and concat the rest.

entries.name: ttnn.experimental.rotary_embedding_hf
entries.notes: Rotation in the HF layout (first half and second half). Use this when the reference calls rotate_half on the checkpoint's own layout and you did not permute the q and k weights.

entries.name: ttnn.experimental.nlp_create_qkv_heads
entries.usage: q, k, v = ttnn.experimental.nlp_create_qkv_heads(xqkv, num_heads=n_heads, num_kv_heads=n_kv, transpose_k_heads=False, memory_config=ttnn.DRAM_MEMORY_CONFIG)
entries.notes: Splits a fused [1, 1, seq, (nh + 2*nkv)*hd] qkv tensor into q [1, nh, seq, hd], k and v [1, nkv, seq, hd]. Prefill form. Set transpose_k_heads=False to keep k as [.., seq, hd].

entries.name: ttnn.experimental.nlp_create_qkv_heads_decode
entries.usage: q, k, v = ttnn.experimental.nlp_create_qkv_heads_decode(xqkv, num_heads=n_heads, num_kv_heads=n_kv, memory_config=mc)
entries.notes: Decode form of the head split (batch in dim 1). Takes a sharded input in the fast path.

entries.name: ttnn.experimental.nlp_concat_heads
entries.notes: [1, nh, seq, hd] back to [1, 1, seq, nh*hd] before the output projection.

entries.name: ttnn.transformer.scaled_dot_product_attention
entries.signature: ttnn.transformer.scaled_dot_product_attention(input_tensor_q, input_tensor_k, input_tensor_v, *, attn_mask=None, is_causal=True, scale=None, sliding_window_size=None, memory_config=None, program_config=None, compute_kernel_config=None)
entries.notes: Prefill attention. k and v may have fewer heads than q (grouped query): do not repeat them yourself. Give only one of attn_mask and is_causal=True. The mask keyword is attn_mask. The sequence must be padded to a multiple of 32.

entries.name: ttnn.transformer.chunk_gated_delta_rule
entries.signature: ttnn.transformer.chunk_gated_delta_rule(q, k, v, g, beta, *, scale=None, initial_state=None, output_final_state=False, chunk_size=64, use_qk_l2norm=False, output_head_major=False, program_config=None, wy_inverse=None, memory_config=None, compute_kernel_config=None, eye=None, tril=None, ones=None, masks=None, num_key_heads=None)
entries.usage: o = ttnn.transformer.chunk_gated_delta_rule(q, k, v, g, beta, chunk_size=32, num_key_heads=2)[0]
entries.notes: Chunked gated delta rule (linear attention) over a prompt. Flat form: q and k [B, T, heads * K], v [B, T, value heads * V], raw (the op normalises q and k and scales q), g and beta [B, T, value heads]; all TILE device tensors. Needs chunk_size 32, T a multiple of 32 and num_key_heads. Returns (o, state): o is [B, T, value heads, V], fp32, ROW_MAJOR (to_layout TILE, then typecast, before a TILE op). Probe 2 matched torch on a chip at 16 and 48 heads (width 128) and 2 and 4 heads (width 64); other shapes are unprobed.

entries.name: ttnn.transformer.scaled_dot_product_attention_decode
entries.signature: ttnn.transformer.scaled_dot_product_attention_decode(input_tensor_q, input_tensor_k, input_tensor_v, *, is_causal=True, attn_mask=None, cur_pos=None, cur_pos_tensor=None, scale=None, sliding_window_size=None, memory_config=None, program_config=None, compute_kernel_config=None)
entries.notes: Decode attention over a dense KV cache. q is [1, batch, heads, hd]. cur_pos_tensor is an int32 device tensor with each user's current position.

entries.name: ttnn.transformer.paged_scaled_dot_product_attention_decode
entries.signature: ttnn.transformer.paged_scaled_dot_product_attention_decode(input_tensor_q, input_tensor_k, input_tensor_v, page_table_tensor, *, is_causal=True, attn_mask=None, cur_pos_tensor=None, scale=None, sliding_window_size=None, memory_config=None, program_config=None, compute_kernel_config=None)
entries.usage: o = ttnn.transformer.paged_scaled_dot_product_attention_decode(q, keys, values, page_table_tensor=page_table, cur_pos_tensor=pos, scale=head_dim ** -0.5)
entries.notes: Decode attention over a paged cache (what vLLM serving uses). Keys and values are the paged cache tensors.

entries.name: ttnn.experimental.paged_update_cache
entries.signature: ttnn.experimental.paged_update_cache(cache_tensor, input_tensor, *, update_idxs=None, update_idxs_tensor=None, share_cache=None, page_table=None, batch_offset=0, compute_kernel_config=None)
entries.notes: Writes one new token per user into the paged cache at its position. Call it for keys and for values. pos is an int32 device tensor.

entries.name: ttnn.experimental.paged_fill_cache
entries.notes: Writes a whole prefill's keys or values into the paged cache. The cache must be reset or overwritten at the start of each request.

entries.name: ttnn.fill_cache
entries.notes: Dense (not paged) cache fill for one user. Use this in a first port that has no page table.

entries.name: ttnn.argmax
entries.notes: Index of the largest value along dim; the output is UINT32. TILE input works for bfloat16 and float32 on the last dim (single core); ROW_MAJOR runs multicore. A port returns logits to the check, so use this only for a serving path.

entries.name: ttnn.topk
entries.signature: ttnn.topk(input_tensor, k=32, dim=-1, largest=True, sorted=True, *, memory_config=None, sub_core_grids=None, indices_tensor=None, output_tensor=None, stable=False)
entries.usage: vals, idx = ttnn.topk(scores, 4, dim=-1, largest=True, sorted=True, stable=True)
entries.notes: Returns (values, indices). The input is TILE on the device; N*C*H must be a multiple of 32 and the last dim is padded to tiles. Among tied scores stable=True takes the lowest index (op probe 7 on a chip: the index list equals the lowest-index rule on every row, k from 4 to 512, deterministic); stable=False is deterministic too but does not follow that rule, and torch.topk does not either (509 of 2557 rows differ on the real-size probe). Read the indices back with to_torch when a mask is built from them.

entries.name: ttnn.sampling
entries.signature: ttnn.sampling(input_values_tensor, input_indices_tensor, *, k, p, temp, seed=None)
entries.usage: tok = ttnn.sampling(vals, idx, k=k_t, p=p_t, temp=inv_t, seed=1234)
entries.notes: Samples an index from the output of topk: softmax over input_values_tensor, then top-k and top-p, then multinomial. k and p are tensors, temp is a tensor holding 1/T, seed is an int. Inputs are bfloat16 TILE.

sections.title: Mesh and collectives (more than one chip)

entries.name: ttnn.open_mesh_device
entries.notes: The check opens the mesh and passes it to `load`; a port does not open one. Shown so you know the shape: (1, N) for N chips in a row.

entries.name: ttnn.ReplicateTensorToMesh
entries.notes: Mapper for from_torch: every chip gets the full tensor.

entries.name: ttnn.ShardTensorToMesh
entries.notes: Mapper for from_torch: dim is split across the chips. Column-parallel weights shard the output dim; row-parallel shard the input dim.

entries.name: ttnn.ConcatMeshToTensor
entries.notes: Composer for to_torch: joins the per-chip shards along dim.

entries.name: ttnn.get_device_tensors
entries.notes: The list of per-chip tensors of a mesh tensor; to_torch each one to read a single chip.

entries.name: ttnn.all_gather
entries.signature: ttnn.all_gather(input_tensor, dim, *, cluster_axis=None, memory_config=None, num_links=None, topology=None)
entries.notes: Joins the shards of a mesh tensor along dim on every chip. Use after a column-parallel matmul whose output feeds a replicated op.

entries.name: ttnn.reduce_scatter
entries.signature: ttnn.reduce_scatter(input_tensor, dim, *, cluster_axis=None, memory_config=None, num_links=None, topology=None)
entries.notes: Sums the partial results of a row-parallel matmul and leaves each chip one slice. Pair with all_gather to get a replicated tensor.

entries.name: ttnn.all_reduce
entries.notes: Sum of the partial results on every chip (reduce_scatter then all_gather in one call). Use it after a row-parallel matmul when the next op needs the full tensor.

entries.name: ttnn.experimental.all_gather_async
entries.signature: ttnn.experimental.all_gather_async(input_tensor, dim, *, multi_device_global_semaphore, num_links=1, memory_config=None, topology=None, cluster_axis=None)
entries.usage: g = ttnn.experimental.all_gather_async(x, dim=3, multi_device_global_semaphore=sem, num_links=1, cluster_axis=1)
entries.notes: The asynchronous form the reference ports use inside traces. It needs global semaphores made once (ttnn.create_global_semaphore). A first port uses the blocking ttnn.all_gather.

mistakes.symptom: `NotImplementedError: prefill not implemented yet` at the first check (run 16).
mistakes.fix: The skeleton raises this in load, prefill, decode_step and close. Write all four before the check runs, even if decode_step first calls prefill on the whole sequence.

mistakes.symptom: `Expected size for first two dimensions of batch2 tensor to be: [6, 32] but got: [6, 6]` (run 18).
mistakes.fix: A matmul between grouped heads of different counts (6 value heads, 2 key heads). Read linear_num_key_heads and linear_num_value_heads with `facts`, repeat the key heads to the value-head count, and print the shapes before each matmul.

mistakes.symptom: `The size of tensor a (32) must match the size of tensor b (8) at non-singleton dimension 3`.
mistakes.fix: Rotary applies to head_dim * partial_rotary_factor (8 of 32 here). Rotate the first part of the head and leave the rest.

mistakes.symptom: `Expected 4-dimensional input for 4-dimensional weight [320, 1, 1, 4], but got 3-dimensional input`.
mistakes.fix: A causal depthwise conv: use torch conv1d with a [C, 1, K] weight, input [B, C, T], left padding K-1 and groups=C. Do not mix a 4-D conv2d weight with a 3-D input.

mistakes.symptom: `SyntaxError: unterminated string literal` at init, after a long write_file.
mistakes.fix: The reply hit the token cap in the middle of the file. Write the port in two or three smaller files or functions and re-read the end of the file after each write.

mistakes.symptom: Top-1 agreement 0.5625 against the 0.85 bar with every op running (runs 16 and 18).
mistakes.fix: Run `stage_tools.py layer-diff` (define layer_outputs in port_model.py) and fix the first layer that differs before touching decode.

mistakes.symptom: A guessed argument that does not exist: `weights=` for embedding, `eps=` or `gamma=` for rms_norm, `mask=` for attention, `bias=` for matmul.
mistakes.fix: The names are weight, epsilon and weight, attn_mask, and bias only on linear.
mistakes.seen_in: CAD benchmark pattern; checked against the tree

mistakes.symptom: `ttnn.conv1d` as a depthwise convolution with dilation above 1 returns a wrong result (PCC 0.2) and raises no error (issue 338).
mistakes.fix: Write the short convolution as shifted multiply-adds: for a kernel of 4 and dilation 3, y = sum_k w[k] * shift(x, (3-k)*3), then silu.

mistakes.symptom: A 4-chip mesh open times out in fabric router sync (run 17, issue 487).
mistakes.fix: A chip link is unhealthy. The port cannot fix it: report it in handoff.json and let the supervisor reset the chips.

mistakes.symptom: `TT_FATAL: Can't convert a tensor distributed on MeshShape([1, 2]) mesh to row-major logical tensor. Supply a mesh composer to concatenate multi-device shards.` at prefill, three times (run 20). The line was `logits = ttnn.to_torch(logits)` or `ttnn.to_torch(weight)` with no composer.
mistakes.fix: On two chips every tensor made with from_torch(..., device=mesh_device) lives on both chips, and to_torch needs a composer to read it back. Use `ttnn.to_torch(t, mesh_composer=ttnn.ConcatMeshToTensor(mesh_device, dim=-1))`. A replicated tensor then comes back n_chips times as wide along that dim: slice the first copy, for example `[..., :vocab_size]` for logits. Keep host copies of weights from load; do not read a weight back inside prefill.

mistakes.symptom: `The width of the first tensor must be equal to the height of the second tensor. Mismatch: width=64 height=320` (also height=384; run 20). 64 is the hidden size; 320 and 384 are the out_features of in_proj_qkv and lm_head.
mistakes.fix: ttnn.linear and ttnn.matmul compute x @ w, not x @ w.T. A torch Linear weight is [out, in], so it was passed as stored. Upload `w_torch.T.contiguous()` once in load, or pass `transpose_b=True`. In the message the first number is the last dim of x and the second is the second-to-last dim of w: when the second equals a weight's out_features, that weight was not transposed.

mistakes.symptom: The device-ops gate fails with `ttnn calls found: ttnn.Parameter x2, ttnn.from_torch x2` although the port has a `ttnn.linear` call, written inside a nested `def ttnn_forward(self, hidden_states)` that replaces `module.forward` (run 20, last repair step).
mistakes.fix: The gate counts calls that load, prefill or decode_step reach. A function that nothing in those paths calls is not reached, and calling the Hugging Face model (`model(input_ids)`) runs its own torch ops on the host even when each Linear.forward is patched. Write the forward pass in port_model.py as functions that take ttnn tensors, and call ttnn.linear from prefill and decode_step or from helpers they call. Keep the weights as plain ttnn tensors in a dict; the port needs no wrapper class for them.

mistakes.symptom: `FAILED: device-ops: after load() the port holds 590095 weight elements as host torch or numpy tensors and 491778 as ttnn tensors; at most 50% may stay on the host` (run 22). The 590095 is close to the whole checkpoint, and the port had uploaded most projections.
mistakes.fix: The check scans everything reachable from the object load returns, so a second host copy counts. Keep each tensor in one place: the device tensor for an uploaded weight, a host tensor for the rest. Do not keep the dict read_tensors returned, or a torch model, on the model object. Choose the weights to upload by shape (2-D, name ends in .weight, not an embedding table) and not by a list of layer names, which misses projections.
mistakes.seen_in: run 22 (load gate, attempt 1); cause inferred from the element counts

mistakes.symptom: The port builds `Qwen4ExpForCausalLM(config)` in load ("Create model on meta device") and uploads `module.weight.data`; the checkpoint tensors it read are never used (run 20, last written port).
mistakes.fix: A model built from the config holds no checkpoint values: its weights are meta or randomly initialised, so the numbers on the device are wrong even when every shape fits. Upload the tensors that read_tensors(model_dir) returns, by name, with ttnn.from_torch(tensor, ...). Do not construct the Hugging Face model in load; the excerpts show the class so you can write the forward pass over those tensors.

mistakes.symptom: `AttributeError: 'ttnn._ttnn.tensor.Tensor' object has no attribute 'view'` (also `.t()`, `.permute(...)`, `.transpose(...)` and `.chunk(...)`).
mistakes.fix: A ttnn tensor has none of these methods. Use the functions: ttnn.reshape(x, shape), ttnn.permute(x, dims), ttnn.transpose(x, a, b), or read the tensor back with _to_host(model, t) and use torch.

mistakes.symptom: `TypeError: bad operand type for unary -: 'ttnn._ttnn.tensor.Tensor'`.
mistakes.fix: Use ttnn.neg(x) or ttnn.multiply(x, -1.0).
mistakes.seen_in: arm E7; ttnn.Tensor operators are listed in ttnn/ttnn/__init__.py (no __neg__)

mistakes.symptom: `TypeError: ttnn.repeat(): incompatible function arguments ... repeat(ttnn.Tensor, int, int, int, int)`.
mistakes.fix: Pass the counts as one tuple: ttnn.repeat(x, (1, 1, 1, n)).

mistakes.symptom: `TypeError: chunk(): argument 'input' must be Tensor, not ttnn._ttnn.tensor.Tensor`, or `torch.arange(..., device=x.device)` on a ttnn tensor.
mistakes.fix: A ttnn tensor is not a torch tensor and has no torch device. Read it back first with `h = _to_host(model, t)`, use torch on h, and upload the result with `_upload(model, h, ttnn.TILE_LAYOUT)`.

mistakes.symptom: `TT_FATAL: ... Input and gamma padded widths must match` from `_rms_norm` on a per-head `q_norm` or `k_norm`.
mistakes.fix: Those weights are head_dim wide and the input is heads * head_dim wide. Reshape x to (1, 1, S * heads, head_dim), call _rms_norm(model, name, x), and reshape back to (1, 1, S, heads * head_dim).

mistakes.symptom: `TypeError: _to_host() missing 1 required positional argument: 't'`, or `_upload() missing ... 'layout'`.
mistakes.fix: The helpers are `_to_host(model, t)` and `_upload(model, t, layout)`; `_upload_ids(model, ids)` takes a list of ints. The model comes first.

mistakes.symptom: `KeyError: 'model.layers.3.self_attn.weight'` raised inside `_linear`.
mistakes.fix: `_linear(model, prefix, x)` reads model['dev'][prefix + '.weight']. Pass the projection's path, such as `model.layers.3.self_attn.q_proj`, and not the block's path. The exact tensor names of a layer are in port_facts.json.

mistakes.symptom: `KeyError: 'model.layers.0.linear_attn.in_proj.weight'`, a `.bias` the checkpoint does not have, or `dt_bias` looked up in `model['host']`.
mistakes.fix: A tensor name is the checkpoint's own: copy it from port_facts.json. A bare parameter such as A_log or dt_bias has no `.weight` suffix.

mistakes.symptom: `KeyError: 'head_k_dim'` or `KeyError: 'num_key_value_groups'` on CONFIG.
mistakes.fix: CONFIG holds exactly the keys of the checkpoint's config; the request lists them. Compute a derived value: groups = CONFIG['num_attention_heads'] // CONFIG['num_key_value_heads'].
mistakes.seen_in: arms E5, E7, E10, E11, E12

mistakes.symptom: `KeyError: 'mesh_device'`, `'n_devices'`, `'ck'`, `'cos_cached'` or `'rotary_emb.cos_cached'`.
mistakes.fix: `model` is a dict with the keys mesh_device, n_devices, dev, host, ids and ck: read model['mesh_device'], not model['dev']['mesh_device']. model['dev'] and model['host'] hold weights only. The rotary tables come from `_rope_tables(model, n)` when the port has it.

mistakes.symptom: `IndexError: Too many indices for tensor of dimension 4`, or a reshape to 5 dimensions followed by a permute with four axes.
mistakes.fix: Keep ttnn activations 4-D. To split heads: ttnn.reshape(x, (1, S, heads, head_dim)), then ttnn.permute(x, (0, 2, 1, 3)) gives [1, heads, S, head_dim]. The reshape of a tile-layout tensor to a last dimension that is not a multiple of 32 has not been checked on a board here: if it complains, read the tensor back with _to_host, split the heads in torch and upload with _upload.

mistakes.symptom: `TT_FATAL` in ttnn.concat about shapes, or in ttnn.slice about a start or end past the dimension.
mistakes.fix: ttnn.concat needs equal shapes in every dimension except dim. A ttnn.slice end must not exceed the dimension and a start must be below it.

mistakes.symptom: `ImportError: attempted relative import with no known parent package`, or `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'port_helpers'`.
mistakes.fix: The port is one file that the check imports by name. Its helpers (_linear, _rms_norm, _upload, _to_host and the others the request lists) are functions in that file: call them. Import only ttnn, torch, math, numpy, re, functools, itertools, typing and collections.

reported.symptom: `ttnn.matmul`, `ttnn.linear` or `minimal_matmul` gives wrong results that change from run to run when the inner dimension K is not a multiple of 32 (the report: bf16 [250, 10] @ [10, 1] was off by 27 to 41 across runs, against 0.95 for a CPU bf16 baseline). The matmul sums over the tile padding of K, and other device ops such as reshape leave that padding non-zero.
reported.fix: Keep K a multiple of 32 where you choose the shape. Otherwise zero the tile padding of both operands before the matmul: `ttnn.fill_implicit_tile_padding` exists in the ttnn 0.79 python package (found by reading its files, not by running it), and the report used it. Compare the first call with torch on the same inputs, twice. Reported on Kohaku-TT's tt-metal build; not reproduced on our pin.
reported.source: Kohaku-TT, docs/reference/ttnn-issues.md (Apache-2.0), seen on that project's tt-metal build

reported.symptom: `ttnn.embedding` returns wrong rows when the index is a TILE-layout int32 tensor made on the device (typecast to uint32, turned to row-major, reshaped to 1-D): in the report 450 of 1000 bf16 rows were wrong. An index uploaded from the host as row-major was exact.
reported.fix: Upload token ids from the host with `ttnn.from_torch(ids, dtype=ttnn.uint32, layout=ttnn.ROW_MAJOR_LAYOUT, ...)`, as the `ttnn.from_torch` entry says. If an index has to be computed on the device, compare the gathered rows with a host `index_select` before you trust them. Reported on Kohaku-TT's tt-metal build; not reproduced on our pin.
reported.source: Kohaku-TT, docs/reference/ttnn-issues.md (Apache-2.0), seen on that project's tt-metal build

reported.symptom: `ttnn.linear` with a bias and no program config fails with TT_FATAL "Broadcast error" when the input has rank above 2 (for example [batch, seq, hidden]).
reported.fix: Reshape the input to 2-D before the call, or call the linear without the bias and add the bias with a separate `ttnn.add`. Print the shapes before the call. Reported on Kohaku-TT's tt-metal build; not reproduced on our pin. It may already work on our version.
reported.source: Kohaku-TT, docs/reference/ttnn-issues.md (Apache-2.0), seen on that project's tt-metal build

reported.symptom: `ttnn.transformer.scaled_dot_product_attention` with fp32 destination accumulation gives wrong outputs when the sequence length is not a multiple of 32: the padding of the last key tile is read as keys.
reported.fix: Use the bf16 destination path for unmasked attention (the report's workaround, which masks that tile), or pad the sequence to a multiple of 32 and mask the padded keys yourself. Check against torch at a length that is not a multiple of 32, such as 58. Reported on Kohaku-TT's tt-metal build; not reproduced on our pin.
reported.source: Kohaku-TT, docs/reference/ttnn-issues.md (Apache-2.0), seen on that project's tt-metal build

reported.symptom: `ttnn.transformer.scaled_dot_product_attention` with many (batch, head) pairs can mix outputs across pairs: for some pairs the result had cosine similarity 0.93 to 0.997 against the same pair computed alone.
reported.fix: When batch times heads is large, split the call into groups of at most 48 pairs (the report's limit) and compare each head's output with torch before you trust the whole tensor. Reported on Kohaku-TT's tt-metal build; not reproduced on our pin.
reported.source: Kohaku-TT, docs/reference/ttnn-issues.md (Apache-2.0), seen on that project's tt-metal build
